cohort: The study included 200 participants with high-risk pregnancies (34 weeks gestation and beyond) divided into ambulatory and nonambulatory groups.
finding: Ambulation during labor in high-risk pregnancies was associated with significantly fewer cases of fetal distress, lower cesarean section rates, and higher APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Ambulation during labor resulted in a lower cesarean section rate (11% vs 22%) and promoted spontaneous vaginal delivery.
